snapshots.subject: Issue-#145 distro whitelist gate wave (feature branch, commit cf6aa85)

findings.summary: Missing /etc/os-release silently kills streamed install (pipefail rc 2, zero output) — the 0.0.39b C2 class.
Gate-call wiring unpinned (0.0.42d class): rewired '_distro_gate unknown' call keeps suite green, pins token-blind.
tr strips only double quotes: single-quoted or CRLF VERSION_ID misses whitelist, falsely refusing supported distros.
Getting-started docs overstate gate: 'refuses everywhere else' — actually unsupported Ubuntu versions only; Debian/Mint pass.
Flag docs imply a Debian 12+ floor is enforced; gate never checks Debian versions (Debian 11 passes).
Point-release VERSION_ID 22.04.3 refused although matrix row reads Ubuntu 22.04 yes; fail-closed, footnote at most.
Suite header still self-describes as parse_args()-only; 18 new gate/order assertions undocumented in header list.
Root performs streamed sibling fetch and sources fetched libs before gate refuses; self-contained gate could precede fetch_kit.
FORCE_UNSUPPORTED_DISTRO clobbered before parse_args: env carry-through dead, CLI-only as documented — support, not security, boundary.
RETRACTED: SIGPIPE sed-to-head rc 141 on huge single-line os-release under pipefail — unreachable, files spec-bound tiny.
RETRACTED: _dg_v/_dg_id leak as shell globals — established underscore pattern, no collision in install.sh.
RETRACTED: terminal-escape injection via raw os-release bytes onto root terminal — requires /etc write, attacker already root.
RETRACTED: sed function-extraction range could truncate on nested brace — no column-0 brace exists in body.
